definitions.gloss: cold sweat; breaking out in a cold sweat
definitions.explanation: Perspiration caused by fear, anxiety, nervousness, or a close call rather than by heat or exertion.

examples.japanese: {危|あぶ}ないところで{冷汗|れいかん}が{出|で}た。
examples.english: I broke into a cold sweat at the close call.

examples.japanese: {上司|じょうし}に{呼|よ}び{出|だ}されたとき、{冷汗|れいかん}が{止|と}まらなかった。
examples.english: When I was called in by my boss, the cold sweat wouldn't stop.

notes:
Composed of {冷|れい} (cold) and {汗|かん} (sweat). The more colloquial form is {冷|ひ}や{汗|あせ} (ひやあせ), which is far more common in everyday speech. {冷汗|れいかん} tends to appear in written or more formal contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {冷汗|れいかん}をかく: to break out in a cold sweat
- {冷汗|れいかん}が{出|で}る: cold sweat comes out
- {冷汗|れいかん}{三斗|さんと}: sweating profusely from fear (idiomatic)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {冷|ひ}や{汗|あせ}: cold sweat — the colloquial equivalent, much more common in speech
- {脂汗|あぶらあせ}: clammy/greasy sweat — sweat from extreme pain or distress
- {寝汗|ねあせ}: night sweat — perspiration during sleep

NOTE ON READINGS:
Do not confuse with {霊感|れいかん} (spiritual sensitivity/inspiration), which is a homophone.
